calibration.policy: exact stable match with forced/forbidden-token control; otherwise abstain
calibration.protocol_note: N001 sent reasoning.enabled=false through OpenRouter; the shipped generic request omits that optional field and was re-smoked on the o200k route.

claim_scope: An exact match is consistent with an enrolled API-visible token-ID namespace. It is not proof of weights, provider, model family, lineage, or exact model identity.
fusion_rule: Correlated with prompt-token tokenizer evidence; do not count it as an independent identity vote.

openai-cl100k.reason: underdetermined: only ID 32 was accepted, and its echo A is shared by smaller vocabularies

limitations: Only openai-o200k is nameable; it has two cross-route holdouts from N001.
The cl100k observation is excluded because the frozen probes do not distinguish it from smaller vocabularies.
Eleven of fifteen N001 routes were ineligible. DeepInfra often ignored the bias; Mistral Small 3.1 on Cloudflare honored it but the fixed ID-32 visible control was non-printing.
The Llama provider control was uninformative: both routes ignored the bias, and transient DeepInfra 429 responses made the reference vector incomplete.
Namespaces can be shared by many checkpoints and can be emulated by a gateway; two holdouts are too few for a useful error-rate bound.
